subject: The Papyrus · A power plant you can see from orbit
html:
Turning the desert's oldest asset into its newest

Near Aswan, where Egypt has always had more sunlight than it knew what to do with, sits Benban Solar Park — a field of panels commonly cited at about 1.8 GW of capacity. When it came online around 2018–2019 it was ranked among the largest solar installations on Earth, big enough to be a landmark from orbit. (Source: Benban Solar Park, Wikipedia.)

Not a one-off

Benban was the anchor, not the whole story. Egypt kept building: Kom Ombo (200 MW, which set a record-low solar tariff), Abydos 1 (500 MW, operational since December 2024), plus large Gulf-of-Suez wind farms like Gabal El Zeit (580 MW). Add the projects up in EgyBI's renewable_projects table and the scale of the shift is a single SUM away. (Sources: AmCham Egypt; project developers.)

The honest asterisk

Superlatives age. By 2025, larger parks in India and China had pushed Benban to roughly third-largest, and some reporting cites about 1.465 GW grid-connected rather than the headline 1.8 GW. Both numbers are in the record, and EgyBI keeps the caveat rather than quietly picking the bigger one — because "one of the largest, as of this date, by this measure" is the truthful shape of almost every superlative.

Five thousand years of sun, finally on the grid. See you next month.
